what: just qc and the code review run in parallel on the same integrated head H; the review verdict names H, not the qc status head H'; the merge ask names H' and both verdicts, and a check proves H to H' changes only the status files. A clean merge of main keeps the qc verdict when a check proves the lane's own diff is unchanged; the merge ask names the judged head, the refreshed head and the proof. The judge is a qc judge with its own role, not a code reviewer. Project rule renamed 'Review and qc judge one head'.
why: Owner ruling, issue #67 items 1, 9 and 10 (Tom, 2026-10-21): QC is every check on what ships; the code reviewer does code quality only; qc and review must not wait on each other, and a clean main refresh must not rerun the judge. Marked weakens because the review verdict no longer names the exact merge head; the status-only check carries that guarantee instead.
evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: docs/adr/0022 (corrected in place, issue #67 item 9: integrate, then qc and review in parallel, then the merge ask) and agents/qc-judge.md (the judge's own role, item 1) against issue-lifecycle#lanes-one-head 'its status-only commit is the head the fresh code review then judges' and #acceptance-qc-interim 'from a code reviewer started fresh'.

what: Parent issues and tickets live in the target's tracker, GitHub Issues or Linear; pull requests and merges stay on GitHub; a Linear lane's PR body says Tracks <KEY> (the tracker skill's pr-line) and the supervisor moves the parent and tickets to done with issue-done after merge; the qc judge runs without a tracker credential. Adds acceptance-merge-linear, acceptance-pr-tracks, acceptance-no-github-issue and story-linear-lane.
why: Owner ruling (2026-10-22, issue #82): the kit works with Linear directly so it can run on a Linear-first repository; the tracker is set per target in .octo-feather.toml, tracker work lives in packaged skills (github-pr, github-issues, linear) behind fixed script names, and ADR 0004 and 0011 were corrected in place to match.
evidence: Corrected ADR 0004 says the tracker is GitHub Issues or Linear, chosen per target, and ADR 0011 that a Linear lane's key is its lowercased ticket key, while the spec as accepted says 'A lane is one merge ask on one parent GitHub issue' (context) and 'GitHub owns parent issues, sub-issues' (boundary-github); the accepted criteria cannot pass on a Linear target.

what: A lane whose brief names no criterion (a fix to a rule an ADR or an owner ruling owns) builds none and runs no just qc: the fresh code review alone judges its integrated head, and its merge ask names that head, links the review verdict, shows checks passing and says the lane builds no criterion (Built: none, no criterion rows). Adds acceptance-merge-ask-no-criterion.
why: Owner, issue #95 (fix it rather than work around it): a lane that claims no criterion states it, and the merge-ask check then requires only the head, checks, review verdict and spec-calls items, with no just qc. One mechanism: the existing merge ask section and octo-feather-lane merge-ask, with Built: none, which the check already reads.
evidence: `octo-feather-lane merge-ask` refused PR #83 (#80), PR #90 (#84) and PR #94 (#93), lanes that build no criterion, with `criterion table: missing` and `Built: no qc: built commit on PR #N; run just qc on the lane head`; each merge ask went up with the refusal quoted (director finding 53). #lanes-one-head as accepted has every lane run just qc naming its criteria, which a lane with none cannot.

what: A ticket that serves no criterion names the rule it serves and that rule's owner, an ADR or an owner ruling, instead of a criterion id, and still ends on a demo; acceptance-one-head applies to a lane that builds at least one criterion.
why: Owner, issue #95 comments (lane #121): defect tickets whose rule an ADR or owner ruling owns cannot be filed as sub-issues. Same mechanism as the review's Check lines, `<rule> (<owner>)` (docs/adr/0008). Marked weakens: a ticket may now name no criterion, and the one-head criterion no longer covers a lane with no qc report. Out of scope: the second #95 example, a gate recipe's demo, which is the demo-surface rule (ADR 0009), a different mechanism.
evidence: `octo-feather-lane ticket` refuses a ticket naming no criterion (`class: no-criterion: no acceptance item names a criterion id`), so #121's check-scripts, check-dashes, check-refs lane-branch and integrate hand-in tickets (rules: docs/adr/0011, docs/adr/0017, owner rulings) could not be filed; and #acceptance-one-head 'the qc report named every criterion the lane builds' against #lanes-one-head's no-criterion lane, which runs no just qc.

what: just qc and the code review both run to their verdicts: one failing first never stops the other, and one implementer repairs the blocking findings of both at once before both run again in parallel on the new head.
why: Owner review comment on #lanes-one-head (2026-10-26): let both finish even if one fails first, so a second failure's problems are addressed in the same repair. Consistent with docs/adr/0022 (a failed verdict of either is a blocking finding, then both run again in parallel).
evidence: #lanes-one-head as accepted says 'neither waits for the other' and 'If either verdict fails, an implementer repairs it and both run again', which leaves open whether a failed qc or review stops the other run before it reports; the owner's review comment asks that both finish.

what: Correction lanes also start on each reflection-missed finding (fix: the question list), and the repeat count covers the director log as well as lane hand-off logs; a correction lane for a class the director reflection routed names that route. The lane close and the merge relay include the lane and director reflections.
why: Owner rulings on issue #230 (2026-10-27, 2026-10-28): the factory introspects itself without the owner as the loop: a fresh cross-family reflector (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, high) reflects at every lane close and on the director's work after each merge relay and at least daily, mines review finding classes across lanes and routes each recurring writer mistake to prevention at the writer, and a gap a reflection missed updates its question list (questions owned once, as data). Reuses pstack reflect (vendored, Pi/Herdr patch). Goes to owner review and Accept before any lane code.
evidence: issue-lifecycle#lanes-correction at main 2e1f97d starts a correction lane only on an owner correction at a gate or a class repeated across lanes, so a gap a reflection missed (issue #230 item 3) changes no question list, and nothing routes a repeated class to its writer: correction lanes #124 and #160 (duplicated-rule) closed and code review logged duplicated-rule again on gh137 and gh149.
